title: Design Plugin Architecture
question: Design a plugin architecture using Spring. Requirements: 1) Dynamically discover and load plugins at startup, 2) Each plugin is a separate JAR with its own Spring context, 3) Plugins can register handlers for specific event types, 4) Parent context should be able to access plugin-provided services, 5) Support hot-reloading of plugins without application restart, 6) Isolate plugin failures from main application. Discuss: using @ComponentScan with custom classpath scanning to discover plugin JARs, creating child ApplicationContext for each plugin with parent-child relationship, using hierarchical contexts where plugins can't see each other but can see parent, implementing plugin interface that all plugins must implement, using ApplicationEventPublisher for plugin communication, implementing custom ClassLoader for each plugin to enable isolation, using @Conditional annotations to enable/disable plugins, implementing plugin versioning and dependency management, using Spring Boot's auto-configuration for plugin initialization, implementing graceful degradation when plugins fail, and testing plugin isolation and communication.

title: Implement Multi-Tenancy
question: Implement multi-tenancy in a Spring application. Requirements: 1) Support multiple tenants with isolated data, 2) Tenant identification from request (header, subdomain, or path), 3) Dynamic datasource routing per tenant, 4) Tenant-specific configuration, 5) Security isolation between tenants, 6) Shared schema with discriminator column OR separate schemas per tenant. Discuss: using AbstractRoutingDataSource to route to tenant-specific datasource, storing tenant ID in ThreadLocal via TenantContext, using HandlerInterceptor or Filter to extract tenant ID from request, implementing TenantIdentifierResolver for Hibernate, using @TenantAware custom annotation to enforce tenant filtering, implementing row-level security using tenant discriminator column, using separate schemas with dynamic schema resolution, caching datasource connections per tenant, implementing tenant provisioning and deprovisioning, using Spring Security for tenant-level authorization, implementing audit logging with tenant information, handling tenant context in async operations using TaskDecorator, and testing tenant isolation.

title: Feature Flag System
question: Design a feature flag system using Spring. Requirements: 1) Enable/disable features at runtime without deployment, 2) Support percentage-based rollouts, 3) Target specific users or user segments, 4) Multiple environments with different flag states, 5) Real-time flag updates without restart, 6) Audit trail of flag changes. Discuss: creating @FeatureFlag annotation for method-level control, implementing FeatureFlag aspect using AOP to intercept flagged methods, using @Conditional annotations to conditionally register beans based on flags, storing flags in database with caching layer (Redis/Caffeine), implementing percentage-based rollout using user hash, creating FeatureFlagService to check flag state with user context, using Spring Cloud Config or external service (LaunchDarkly, Unleash) for flag management, implementing A/B testing with flag variants, using @Profile for environment-specific flag defaults, implementing real-time flag updates using Spring Cloud Bus or polling, adding metrics to track feature flag usage, and graceful fallback when flags are unavailable.

title: Circuit Breaker Pattern Implementation
question: Implement circuit breaker pattern for resilient microservices. Requirements: 1) Protect downstream service calls from cascading failures, 2) Automatic state transitions (closed → open → half-open), 3) Configurable failure threshold and timeout, 4) Fallback mechanisms, 5) Metrics and monitoring, 6) Thread isolation. Discuss: using Resilience4j @CircuitBreaker annotation on service methods, configuring failure rate threshold and wait duration, implementing fallback methods with same signature, using @TimeLimiter for timeout protection, using @Bulkhead for thread isolation, implementing health indicators to expose circuit breaker state, using Micrometer to publish circuit breaker metrics, configuring different circuit breakers for different downstream services, implementing retry with exponential backoff using @Retry, combining circuit breaker with rate limiting, testing circuit breaker state transitions, and handling partial failures in batch operations.

title: Build Custom Spring Boot Starter
question: Create a custom Spring Boot starter for a common library. Requirements: 1) Auto-configuration for easy integration, 2) Configurable properties with sensible defaults, 3) Conditional bean registration based on classpath, 4) Configuration metadata for IDE support, 5) Minimal dependencies, 6) Documentation and examples. Discuss: creating starter module (my-library-spring-boot-starter) and autoconfigure module (my-library-spring-boot-autoconfigure), implementing @AutoConfiguration class with conditional annotations, using @ConfigurationProperties for externalized configuration, generating spring-configuration-metadata.json using annotation processor, registering auto-configuration in META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports (Spring Boot 3) or spring.factories (Spring Boot 2), using @ConditionalOnClass to check for required dependencies, using @ConditionalOnMissingBean to allow user overrides, implementing proper ordering with @AutoConfigureBefore/@AutoConfigureAfter, providing default beans for common use cases, adding comprehensive JavaDoc and README, creating sample application demonstrating usage, and publishing to Maven Central or private repository.

title: Event-Driven Decoupling
question: Refactor a monolithic application to event-driven architecture using Spring. Requirements: 1) Decouple modules using domain events, 2) Async event processing, 3) Event persistence and replay, 4) Guaranteed delivery, 5) Event versioning, 6) Dead letter queue for failed events. Discuss: defining domain events extending ApplicationEvent, using @EventListener or @TransactionalEventListener for handlers, using @Async for asynchronous processing, implementing event store using database table for persistence, using Spring Modulith for module boundaries, integrating with message broker (RabbitMQ/Kafka) for distributed events, implementing outbox pattern to ensure atomic event publishing with database transaction, using @TransactionalEventListener(phase = AFTER_COMMIT), versioning events using event version field and maintaining backward compatibility, implementing event upcasting for version migration, creating dead letter queue for failed event processing, implementing retry with exponential backoff, using idempotency tokens to handle duplicate events, and monitoring event processing lag.

title: Advanced Caching Strategy
question: Design an advanced caching strategy for a high-traffic application. Requirements: 1) Multi-level caching (L1: local, L2: distributed), 2) Cache warming on startup, 3) Selective cache invalidation, 4) Cache stampede prevention, 5) Time-based and event-based eviction, 6) Monitoring and metrics. Discuss: using @Cacheable with Caffeine for L1 cache and Redis for L2 cache, configuring CacheManager with cache-through strategy, implementing cache warming using @PostConstruct or ApplicationReadyEvent, using @CacheEvict with condition for selective invalidation, implementing cache-aside pattern with @Cacheable, using @CachePut for write-through caching, preventing cache stampede using Redisson's distributed lock, implementing probabilistic early expiration to avoid thundering herd, using Spring's cache abstraction with multiple cache managers, publishing cache metrics to Prometheus, implementing cache version tags for bulk invalidation, using @Caching to combine multiple cache operations, handling null values and empty collections, implementing cache synchronization across instances using Spring Cloud Bus or Redis pub/sub, and testing cache behavior with different failure scenarios.

title: Graceful Shutdown Implementation
question: Implement graceful shutdown for a Spring Boot application. Requirements: 1) Complete in-flight requests before shutdown, 2) Stop accepting new requests, 3) Close database connections and external resources, 4) Send shutdown signal to load balancer, 5) Configurable shutdown timeout, 6) Clean up background tasks. Discuss: enabling graceful shutdown with server.shutdown=graceful, configuring spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase, implementing ApplicationListener<ContextClosedEvent> for cleanup, using @PreDestroy on beans for resource cleanup, implementing SmartLifecycle for controlled stop of background tasks with phases, draining ExecutorService using shutdown() and awaitTermination(), closing database connection pools properly, deregistering from service registry before shutdown, implementing health check endpoint that returns OUT_OF_SERVICE during shutdown, using SignalHandler to catch SIGTERM, implementing idempotent operations to handle interrupted requests, adding shutdown hooks using Runtime.addShutdownHook() for critical cleanup, configuring timeout for force kill, logging shutdown progress, and testing with load testing tool during deployment.
